title: Satyakama and His Mother's Truth
text:
A boy named Satyakama wanted to become a student of the Vedas. A student had to give the name of his family line, so he asked his mother, Jabala, what his lineage was.

She told him honestly that she did not know. When she was young, she said, she had worked as a servant and moved about a great deal, and she had conceived him then. All she could tell him was that her name was Jabala and his was Satyakama. He should simply call himself Satyakama Jabala.

The boy went to the teacher Haridrumata Gautama and asked to be accepted. When Gautama asked about his family, Satyakama repeated exactly what his mother had said, without hiding anything.

Gautama answered that no one but a true brahmin could speak so plainly. "Bring the firewood, my son. I will initiate you, because you have not departed from the truth." He then gave the boy four hundred thin, weak cows and sent him off to tend them. Satyakama vowed not to return until they had become a thousand. He spent years in the wilderness, and by the time he came back with the herd, the Upanishad says, his face shone with knowledge.
lesson: Honesty about awkward family facts is a strength, not a shame. A child who can tell the truth plainly has learned what matters most.
people: Satyakama, his mother Jabala, the teacher Haridrumata Gautama
